title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Opening page of a 1986 manuscript, 'Analysis situs (première mouture)', labelled 'GF IV'. Its declared aim is to give a 'set-theoretic topological' model of the combinatorics of a 'topological shape model' (modèle de forme topologique), in the case of a 'construit' (built object). This is the tame-topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5–6).

The ambient material is an 'espace ± ordinaire' E. It can be either:
- a Hausdorff topological space, or
- a 'tame space' (espace modéré), not necessarily compact, relative to a 'given tame theory'. The tame theory is a parameter, much like a choice of o-minimal structure.

In the tame case, 'closed subset' means 'tame closed subset'.

Definition (Figures). A figure F of E consists of a closed subset X = |F| (its support), together with a decomposition X = ∪ X_i into closed parts X_i, called the closed strata. The image writes 'décomposition de Y' and '{X_i} ∈ 𝔓(Y)', evidently a slip for X. The hypotheses are:
- (added) the X_i are non-empty and locally connected.
- a) the X_i are closed and X = ∪ X_i.
- b) the family (X_i) is locally finite.
- Margin: the strata form a poset, with i ≤ j ⇔ X_i ⊂ X_j and i < j ⇔ X_i ⊊ X_j.
- c) if X_i ⊊ X_j, then X_i is rare (nowhere dense) in X_j.
- d) set the boundary ∂X_i = ∪_{j<i} X_j. By the next page, this is closed by a)–c), and the 'interior' X_i° = X_i \ ∂X_i is required to be (1) a manifold (a tame manifold in the tame setting) and (2) connected.
- e) (margin, next page) a compatibility of X_i < X_j with ∂X_j.
- f) X_i ∩ X_j is a union of strata.

Modern reading. A figure is a locally finite stratification with connected manifold strata satisfying the frontier condition. It is encoded by the closures of the strata (the 'closed strata') rather than the strata themselves. The figure is therefore identified with its set of closed strata, F ⊂ 𝒫_f(X), whose poset Σ_F is the stratification poset.

The next page then considers:
- a chosen set 𝓕 of admissible figures;
- the total set Σ = ∐_{F ∈ 𝓕} Σ_F → 𝓕 of pairs (F, X_i).

This sets up a combinatorial bookkeeping of figures and their strata posets, as a combinatorial model of shape.

Implicit consequences (check):
- Local finiteness plus c) make ∂X_i a locally finite union of closed nowhere-dense subsets of X_i. Hence ∂X_i is closed and nowhere dense, so X_i° is open and dense in X_i, and X_i is the closure of its open stratum.
- f) plus local finiteness give each x ∈ X a unique minimal closed stratum containing it. If two were minimal, their intersection would be a union of strata, one of which contains x and lies in both. Then x lies in that stratum's open part.
- So the open strata X_i° partition X, and the frontier condition holds. The definition is coherent and is equivalent to the usual notion of a stratification with connected strata satisfying the frontier condition.
errors: 'Décomposition de Y', '{X_i} ∈ 𝔓(Y)' should read X (notational slip in the manuscript).

In the purely topological (non-tame) case, the hypotheses do not prevent pathologies. Strata could be wild manifolds and closures badly embedded, so the 'combinatorial model' would not determine homotopy type without extra (e.g. conical / Whitney-type) conditions. Grothendieck's choice of a tame theory is presumably meant to remedy this; it is not a logical error.
Condition (d) is only stated on the next page. The page itself breaks off at the definition of ∂X_i.

ideas.what: Figure = closed subset with a locally finite decomposition into closed strata, ordered by inclusion, with smaller strata nowhere dense in larger ones, connected manifold interiors, and intersections being unions of strata
ideas.modern_name: Stratified space with frontier condition (closed-strata description); stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (1960s–70s); in the tame setting, o-minimal stratification/cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1984–86)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 sketches tame stratified structures in general terms, without this formal definition

ideas.what: Ambient 'espace modéré' relative to a 'théorie modérée donnée', the tame theory being a parameter
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1984–86); programme announced by Grothendieck, Esquisse 1984

ideas.what: Encoding a figure by its set of closed strata F ∈ 𝒫(𝒫_f(X)), the set of figures 𝓕, and the total stratum set Σ = ∐ Σ_F → 𝓕 as combinatorial data of a shape
ideas.modern_name: Stratification poset / face poset as combinatorial model of a stratified space (cf. exit-path categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson; Treumann; Lurie (Higher Algebra, appendix A); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

missed.claim: Beginning of an axiomatic, set-theoretic foundation of 'modèles de forme' via stratified figures in a parametrized tame theory. The page fixes a set 𝓕 of admissible figures and the total stratum set Σ → 𝓕, aiming at a combinatorial model of shapes ('construits'). This is a concrete unpublished first draft of the Esquisse tame-topology programme. Whether its later development anticipates anything (e.g. stratum posets as combinatorial models of homotopy types, in the spirit of exit-path categories) cannot be judged from this page.
missed.quote: Comme modèle "ensembliste topologique" de la combinatoire d'un "modèle de forme topologique" (cas d'un "construit")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents how Grothendieck intended to formalize tame topology after the Esquisse, in parallel with the independent rise of o-minimality. Possibly a different (figure/poset-based) axiomatics than o-minimal cell decomposition.

deep.surprise_reason: The definition itself is a standard stratification with frontier condition. What is notable is that it is an unpublished 1986 attempt to found the Esquisse tame-topology programme, with the tame theory as a parameter, at the very time o-minimality was emerging. That gives historical interest, but the mathematics on this page is not new.
transcription_corrections: 'd'une "modèle de forme"' should be 'd'un "modèle de forme topologique"' (the word 'topologique' is inserted above the line).
'considérons les notions suivantes' is plausible; the next word reads 'Matériau :' introducing E.
'Une figure F/de E est une partie fermée X, [...] et une décomposition de Y en parties X_i': the image indeed shows Y, evidently meaning X.
Left margin, roughly: 'X est appelé le support de la figure, noté |F|'.
In a), the parenthesis may read '(pas néc. compacts)' rather than '(pas nécessairement connexes)'; uncertain.
Insertion above a): 'non vides et loc. connexes', with a bracketed remark about the case E locally (connected/compact); uncertain.
d): 'Posant ∂X_i = ∪_{j<i} X_j' (the dot is a boundary notation), continued on next page.
